runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets sold off sharply overnight as renewed U.S. military strikes against Iran sent oil prices surging and ignited a broad risk-off rotation across the region. Japan's Nikkei 225 led regional losses, tumbling 2.60% (-1,720 points) to 64,495 — the steepest single-session decline in three months — as higher energy import costs hammered Japanese corporates and a safe-haven yen rally pressured export earnings. New Zealand markets were in focus ahead of an expected RBNZ rate hike decision, while Australia braced for Q2 GDP data (consensus: +0.2–0.4% q/q).

European markets opened cautiously negative Wednesday morning, with Germany's DAX declining 1.02% to 25,990 and the FTSE 100 opening largely flat at 10,789 before modest intraday weakness. European energy companies and defense stocks provided partial offsets to broad-based selling in technology and rate-sensitive sectors. The ECB is closely monitoring oil-driven pass-through risks to core inflation as elevated Brent prices risk re-anchoring expectations at uncomfortable levels heading into autumn monetary policy meetings.

U.S. futures are mixed ahead of Wednesday's open: Dow futures add ~87 points (+0.2%) while Nasdaq 100 futures slip 0.3%, with the 10-year Treasury yield holding at 4.814% — its highest level since November 2023. Sticky inflation (CPI 3.4% y/y, core 2.5%) combined with higher oil is reinforcing Fed hawkishness and the ~70% market-implied probability of a 25bp hike at the September 15-16 FOMC. Tuesday's close marked the S&P 500's third consecutive daily decline to 7,631 (-0.71%), with Nasdaq off 1.03% to 26,100. Pre-market flow clearly favors energy and defense rotation while cybersecurity, semiconductors, and crypto face continued selling pressure.

ideas.catalyst: U.S. military strikes against Iran sent WTI oil near $87/bbl, directly boosting upstream operator margins.
ideas.thesis: Occidental's high leverage to oil prices means each $5/bbl increase adds approximately $500M in annual operating income at current production volumes. With geopolitical risk premium likely to persist and Berkshire Hathaway backstopping shareholder confidence, OXY offers the cleanest pure-play oil upside.
ideas.key_risk: Swift diplomatic resolution or OPEC production increase could reverse the oil premium and sharply compress OXY's stock.

ideas.catalyst: U.S. strikes against Iran signal sustained Middle East military engagement, accelerating precision weapons draw-down and replenishment orders.
ideas.thesis: Lockheed is the primary supplier of F-35s, HIMARS, and precision-guided munitions that form the backbone of U.S. Middle East operations. Historical precedent shows that sustained military engagements trigger supplemental Pentagon appropriations that flow disproportionately to Tier-1 defense primes with active production lines.
ideas.key_risk: Congressional budget impasse or unexpected diplomatic ceasefire could delay contract acceleration.

ideas.catalyst: 10-year yield at 4.814% (highest since Nov 2023) with ~70% market probability of 25bp Fed hike September 15-16.
ideas.thesis: Sticky core inflation at 2.5%, oil-driven headline CPI reacceleration, and a Fed that has telegraphed a September hike combine to make long-duration treasuries acutely vulnerable. TLT's ~17-year duration means even a 25bp rise in yields translates to roughly 4%+ price decline, and the trajectory is for further yield normalization.
ideas.key_risk: A severe risk-off flight to safety could spike treasury demand and cause a violent short squeeze.

ideas.catalyst: William Blair upgraded GTLB to Market Perform from Underperform; stock surging +19.36% in pre-market on strong Q2 results beat.
ideas.thesis: GitLab's integrated AI-assisted DevSecOps platform is winning enterprise consolidation deals as companies rationalize point solutions. The upgrade removes a prominent bearish overhang and the earnings beat demonstrates that competitive pressure from GitHub Copilot has been less damaging than feared.
ideas.key_risk: Broader Nasdaq selloff driven by rate fears could overwhelm single-stock upgrade momentum and reverse the gap fill.

ideas.catalyst: Iran conflict escalation and oil-driven inflation spike simultaneously boost gold's dual safe-haven and inflation-hedge appeal.
ideas.thesis: Gold benefits from a rare dual catalyst: geopolitical risk premium from active U.S.-Iran military engagement and persistent above-target inflation that caps real rate upside even as nominal rates climb. Central bank demand from EM central banks remains a structural floor under spot prices.
ideas.key_risk: A sharp DXY rally driven by safe-haven dollar demand could cap gold gains; diplomatic breakthrough reduces geopolitical premium quickly.

ideas.catalyst: JPMorgan upgraded MLM to Overweight from Neutral with a $680 price target, citing strong H2 2026 volume and pricing guidance.
ideas.thesis: Martin Marietta is the dominant U.S. aggregates supplier with pricing power insulated from commodity volatility by the nature of crushed stone logistics. IIJA infrastructure spending tailwinds continue to drive robust demand for highway and bridge projects through 2027, providing earnings visibility that supports a premium multiple.
ideas.key_risk: Rising interest rates slow residential and commercial construction, reducing aggregate volumes and pressuring the stock despite infrastructure tailwinds.

ideas.catalyst: CRWD down 7.70% Tuesday in sector-wide cybersecurity selloff as rising rates compress premium growth multiples.
ideas.thesis: CrowdStrike trades at approximately 15-18x forward revenue, making it acutely sensitive to discount rate expansion. With the September FOMC hike now near-certain and the 10-year above 4.8%, long-duration software multiples face continued rerating pressure even as underlying ARR growth remains healthy.
ideas.key_risk: A high-profile cyber incident on critical infrastructure could trigger emergency government contracts and immediately reverse institutional selling.

ideas.catalyst: COIN down 6.23% Tuesday as rising rates, geopolitical risk, and three consecutive equity losses accelerate crypto risk-off selling.
ideas.thesis: Coinbase's transaction revenue is directly correlated with crypto trading volumes, which historically contract sharply during equity risk-off periods. Rising rates reduce the relative attractiveness of zero-yield crypto assets, while hawkish Fed rhetoric ahead of September FOMC is a near-term volume headwind.
ideas.key_risk: Bitcoin could decouple from equities and rally as a geopolitical safe-haven or digital gold narrative, sharply boosting COIN volumes.

ideas.catalyst: Deutsche Bank upgraded SIRI to Buy from Hold with a $45 price target, citing undervalued subscriber economics and recurring cash flow.
ideas.thesis: Sirius XM's subscription-based revenue model with locked-in automotive OEM contracts provides recession-resistant recurring cash flows that are underappreciated in the current macro environment. At current levels, the stock trades at a significant discount to Deutsche Bank's intrinsic value estimate.
ideas.key_risk: Subscriber churn in new vehicle sales could disappoint if auto demand weakens under higher rate pressure; streaming audio competition remains a secular headwind.

The proposal represents a dramatic strategic pivot away from GameStop's brick-and-mortar gaming retail roots toward the broader online commerce platform market.

The company's unique positioning at the intersection of AI compute demand and energy infrastructure has attracted top-tier strategic investors.

deals.description: Westinghouse Electric is actively working toward an initial public offering, positioning itself to capitalize on the nuclear power revival driven by AI data center power demand and clean energy policy. The company's AP1000 reactor technology and existing global installed base make it a prime beneficiary of the nuclear renaissance.
deals.sentiment: Bullish for nuclear theme; positive proxy via CCJ and BWXT ahead of Westinghouse listing

runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets closed mostly lower Tuesday as geopolitical tensions spiked after two oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz were struck by projectiles overnight, marking a sharp escalation in the six-month U.S.-Iran conflict. The Nikkei 225 declined 277 points, or 0.42%, closing at 66,129 as Japanese exporters and risk assets sold off broadly. Risk-off sentiment cascaded across the region, with crude oil pushing above $88/barrel on supply disruption fears — the sharpest single-session spike in months and a direct inflation shock to import-dependent Asian economies.

European bourses opened cautiously lower as the continent faces rising energy costs and elevated global bond yields. The DAX shed approximately 0.31% to around 20,650, while the FTSE 100 slipped roughly 0.22% to near 8,824. European defense names partially offset broader weakness, but rising energy prices are fanning inflation concerns across the eurozone. The European Central Bank faces renewed scrutiny over its policy path as imported inflation risks build — a dynamic directly mirroring the pressure now bearing down on the Federal Reserve ahead of its September 17 meeting.

U.S. futures are solidly in the red to open September, historically the weakest month for equities. S&P 500 futures are off 0.6%, Dow futures have shed roughly 335 points (-0.61%), and Nasdaq-100 futures lead the decline at -1.2% as technology faces dual headwinds: rising discount rates and an intensifying domestic AI data center policy debate. Nvidia is down 1.8% to $216.91 pre-market, with Micron (-2.2%) and SanDisk (-2.9%) tracking lower. VIX at 22.4 signals heightened anxiety. The Federal Reserve's September 17 FOMC meeting has taken on new significance as energy-driven inflation complicates the rate path, with 68 economic events scheduled today adding further volatility risk.

ideas.catalyst: Two oil tankers struck in the Strait of Hormuz overnight as U.S.-Iran hostilities escalate, directly threatening one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints.
ideas.thesis: The Strait of Hormuz handles approximately 20% of global oil trade, and escalating military confrontation introduces a genuine supply disruption premium into crude prices. With WTI already above $88/barrel pre-market, any further escalation or tanker interdictions could send prices materially higher in the near term.
ideas.key_risk: A ceasefire or diplomatic de-escalation could rapidly unwind the geopolitical risk premium built into oil prices.

ideas.catalyst: Renewed U.S.-Iran military conflict in the Strait of Hormuz drives expectations for increased U.S. defense procurement and weapons system deployments.
ideas.thesis: Active U.S. military engagement historically precedes accelerated DoD spending and Congressional emergency defense appropriations. Lockheed Martin, as the world's largest defense contractor and supplier of F-35s, THAAD, and Patriot systems, stands directly in line for any increased procurement cycle driven by the ongoing conflict.
ideas.key_risk: Conflict de-escalation or a Congressional budget impasse could limit near-term defense spending upside.

ideas.catalyst: Geopolitical escalation in the Middle East combined with rising inflation expectations from oil's surge drives safe haven flows into gold.
ideas.thesis: Gold benefits from a dual tailwind: risk-off safe haven demand from the U.S.-Iran conflict and an inflation hedge against rising oil-driven CPI. With the 10-year yield at 4.72% and WTI above $88, gold's geopolitical premium is strengthening alongside deteriorating market sentiment entering September.
ideas.key_risk: Further U.S. dollar strength and a hawkish Fed repricing could cap gold gains despite the geopolitical bid.

ideas.catalyst: Nvidia is trading down 1.8% to $216.91 in pre-market as the tech sector faces dual pressure from rising bond yields and an intensifying domestic debate over AI data center policy and energy consumption.
ideas.thesis: Nvidia faces near-term multiple compression risk as 10-year yields push toward 4.72%, reducing the present value of long-duration growth cash flows. Rising political scrutiny of AI data center energy consumption could dampen hyperscaler capex guidance — the primary driver of Nvidia's revenue growth — in the near term.
ideas.key_risk: Any positive AI data center policy development or a surprise dovish Fed pivot could reverse the selloff quickly and sharply.

ideas.catalyst: Morgan Stanley raised Robinhood to Overweight from Equal Weight, lifting the price target to $150 from $124 — a 21% PT increase reflecting confidence in the platform's expanding product suite.
ideas.thesis: Morgan Stanley's upgrade reflects growing conviction in Robinhood's product diversification into crypto, retirement accounts, and UK expansion. Elevated VIX and today's sharp market selloff historically drive retail trading volume and fee revenue on Robinhood's platform, creating a near-term revenue tailwind.
ideas.key_risk: A sustained market downturn reducing retail investor activity could undermine volume-based revenue projections despite the upgrade.

ideas.catalyst: Evercore ISI upgraded Duolingo to Outperform from In Line and doubled the price target to $210 from $105, citing AI-driven product velocity and accelerating user monetization.
ideas.thesis: Duolingo's integration of AI-native learning features has accelerated daily active user growth and subscription revenue. The doubled price target from a major sell-side firm signals a material reassessment of the company's long-term earnings power and competitive moat in the global language learning market.
ideas.key_risk: A broad tech selloff could temporarily overwhelm the stock-specific upgrade catalyst in this risk-off session.

ideas.catalyst: Piper Sandler upgraded Akamai to Overweight from Neutral with a new $125 price target, citing improving cloud security demand and stabilizing CDN pricing dynamics.
ideas.thesis: Akamai's pivot toward cloud security and edge computing positions it to benefit from rising enterprise cybersecurity spend. Rising geopolitical tensions, including the U.S.-Iran conflict, often accelerate enterprise demand for DDoS protection and edge security services — both core Akamai product lines.
ideas.key_risk: Intensifying competition from Cloudflare and Fastly in edge and CDN markets could limit Akamai's revenue re-acceleration.

ideas.catalyst: Global bond yields are rising sharply as oil-driven inflation fears mount and Fed rate hike concerns intensify ahead of the September 17 FOMC meeting.
ideas.thesis: With WTI crude pushing above $88 on Strait of Hormuz supply disruption fears and U.S. CPI already above target, the Fed faces renewed pressure to maintain restrictive policy or hike again. Rising yields hit long-duration bonds hardest, making TLT a high-conviction tactical short as the 10-year yield tests 4.72% and threatens to break higher.
ideas.key_risk: A sharp equity market selloff or flight-to-safety bid could compress yields and drive TLT higher despite the inflation pressure backdrop.

ideas.catalyst: Micron is down 2.2% in pre-market, tracking Nvidia's 1.8% decline as the semiconductor sector faces broad selling pressure amid tech rotation and rising rate fears.
ideas.thesis: Micron is highly cyclical and sensitive to both the macro rate environment and AI capex spending trends. With Nvidia under pressure on AI data center policy concerns, downstream memory demand expectations could be revised lower, hitting Micron's near-term pricing and volume outlook.
ideas.key_risk: Strong guidance updates or positive AI demand data from hyperscalers could quickly reverse the sector-wide selloff.

ideas.catalyst: U.S.-Iran military conflict escalation boosts expectations for Raytheon missile systems and Patriot air defense deployment orders as U.S. forces engage in the Strait of Hormuz region.
ideas.thesis: RTX's Raytheon division is a primary supplier of Patriot missile systems, Tomahawk cruise missiles, and air defense infrastructure — all assets seeing increased demand as U.S. forces engage in the region. International allies' air defense procurement also accelerates during active conflict periods, providing a multi-year order backlog catalyst.
ideas.key_risk: Conflict de-escalation, Congressional gridlock on defense supplementals, or supply chain constraints could limit near-term upside.

deals.headline: SpaceX Acquires xAI in All-Stock Mega-Deal
deals.description: SpaceX completed its acquisition of Elon Musk's xAI artificial intelligence company in a landmark all-stock transaction, creating a vertically integrated AI and space technology conglomerate. The deal consolidates xAI's Grok large language model and compute infrastructure with SpaceX's Starlink satellite network, positioning the combined entity as a major challenger in enterprise AI services.

deals.headline: Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery Complete Merger
deals.description: The long-anticipated combination of Paramount Global and Warner Bros. Discovery closed in the first half of 2026, creating the world's second-largest streaming and traditional media company by content library. The merged entity will operate under a unified streaming platform strategy to compete directly with Netflix and Disney+ in the intensifying streaming wars.

deals.headline: Honeywell Completes Aerospace Spinoff — HONA Begins Trading
deals.description: Honeywell completed the spinoff of its aerospace division on June 29, 2026, with Honeywell Aerospace Technologies (HONA) beginning regular-way trading as an independent pure-play aerospace supplier. The remaining Honeywell Technologies (HON) executed a 1-for-2 reverse split and retains the industrial automation and building solutions businesses.

deals.headline: Oura Smart Ring IPO — September 2026 Target
deals.description: Oura, the Finnish health wearable maker known for its smart ring technology, is targeting a September 2026 IPO following an August Bloomberg report confirming the company's timeline. Oura has seen significant growth in its health-monitoring subscription model and counts high-profile athletes and celebrities among its users.

deals.headline: Anthropic Files Confidentially for IPO — September Window in Play
deals.description: Anthropic, the AI safety company and maker of the Claude large language model family, filed confidentially for an IPO on June 1, 2026, with prediction market participants pricing a September 2026 launch at 46% probability. The company is backed by Google, Amazon, and Spark Capital and is valued at over $60 billion.
